Server: Microsoft-IIS/10.0

findings.title: Web Server Version Disclosure
findings.description: HTTP headers disclose web server or framework technology details.
findings.remediation: Suppress Server and X-Powered-By headers at the edge proxy.

findings.title: HTTP Server Header Disclosure
findings.description: The HTTP response discloses a Server header that reveals the web server product and often a version string. Attackers use this for targeted exploit selection.
findings.evidence:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: Microsoft-IIS/10.0
X-Powered-By: ASP.NET
findings.remediation: Remove or obfuscate the Server header at the reverse proxy or application layer. Prefer a generic value and keep components patched.

findings.title: Missing HTTP Security Headers (Cleartext)
findings.description: Cleartext HTTP is missing framing/MIME-sniffing protections. Prefer redirecting clients to HTTPS.
findings.evidence:
Missing: (?i)x-content-type-options:, (?i)x-frame-options:, (?i)content-security-policy:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: Microsoft-IIS/10.0
X-Powered-By: ASP.NET
findings.remediation: Terminate TLS and emit a full secure header set.

findings.title: Missing Common HTTP Security Headers
findings.description: One or more widely recommended HTTP security headers were not observed in the response. Missing headers increase risk of clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and related client-side attacks.
findings.evidence:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: Microsoft-IIS/10.0
X-Powered-By: ASP.NET
Missing patterns: (?i)strict-transport-security:, (?i)x-content-type-options:, (?i)x-frame-options:, (?i)content-security-policy:
findings.remediation: Configure the web server or reverse proxy to emit HSTS (HTTPS only), X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options (or CSP frame-ancestors), and a Content-Security-Policy appropriate for the application.

findings.title: SMB Service Reachable
findings.description: SMB is reachable; SMBv1 capability was not confirmed from the banner.
findings.remediation: Ensure SMBv1 is disabled and access is network-restricted.
